text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- By signing peace accord with Chechnya, President Boris Yeltsin has recognised its independence.
- A 51 percent stake of Russia's seventh biggest oil producer Sibneft has gone to an industry investment company Finansovaya Neftyanaya Kompania (FNK) after a tender.
- Boris Yeltsin signed on Monday a decree on strengthening state control over Russia's gas monopoly Gazprom.
- Moscow government has started a roadshow in western markets of its eurobonds worth $500 million.
- Tatyana Paramonova, former acting head of Russia's Central Bank, has accepted the post of the first deputy chairman of Elbim-bank, Russia's 99th biggest bank.
SEGODNYA
- Moscow and Chechnya signed a peace accord as two independent states.
- Hundreds of people in Vladivostok took to the streets on Monday to protest against frequent power cuts and unpaid wages.
- Increased rates for traffic fines appears to have increased the number of traffic police on Moscow's streets. There are 10 policemen for each car now, a taxi driver is quoted by the paper.
- World chess champion has fallen victim to "Terminator", says the paper, commenting on Gary Kasparov's defeat to computer Deep Blue.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The text of the peace accord between Russia and Chechnya can be interpreted in any way but it does not seem to be the last page of the Russian-Chechen drama yet.

- Boris Yeltsin is due to sign a Russia-NATO treaty, the text of which must be ready by May 27. It is a matter of honour, says the paper, commenting on the arrival in Moscow on Tuesday of NATO Secretary General Javier Solana.
SOVIETSKAYA ROSSIA
- Western politicians are shocked by the process of unification of former Soviet republics and are stirring up passions over human right in Belarus, says Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov is expecting Russia to finance the Chechen economy in exchange for peace accord with Moscow, says the paper.
- Moscow police arrested a couple who were selling their baby son for $23,000.
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
